title: Joining the Martel band in 1924 at five dollars a night
summary: Joe and his brother hired Bert and Dayton Martel for a three-day convention job, then Albert Martel hired Joe as clarinetist at five dollars a night and he left the shoe shop.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Martel. And my brother got this job to pay for this Catholic Knights of ...(?)... Convention, but we only could get together three pieces, I remember. We had a banjo and we had drums, and myself and my brother, which played the violin. And he knew Bert, the trumpet player; he had met him someplace on Lake Charles...

Yeah, Bert Martel that played trumpet with that family band. And he called him or something, and told him that if he wasn't working those three days... It was the beginning of the week, I guess, because the Martel Band always worked on weekends. I guess maybe this was Monday and Tuesday and Wednesday, it had to be what year...in 1924.
I was going to say... You said you called him, so telephones must have been out certainly.
Yeah, 1924. And asked him could him and Dayton, who was the trombone player, work with us those three days, and they said yes.
So you were 18 at that time.
Yes. So I was still in Baton Rouge, working in the shoe shop with Papa, me and Frank, and my older brother had left and opened a shop of his own in Baton Rouge.

Yes. Time had passed. Anyway, they worked with us for the three days. In the meantime, Martel had a job for two days, and he asked me...old man Albert asked me, he said, 'What are you going to do...' I think the last night we worked... We didn't work at night, we played in the daytime and out in the open. He said, 'I need a clarinet player. Could you play with us for two days
here?" He had a job in Ville Platte(?) and Beaubridge(?), Louisiana. I said... Ville Platte(?) is the east of New Orleans, isn't it?
That was a long ways for you to go then, I guess.
Well, no. Ville Platte(?) is right around there, not far from Lafayette and New Iberia and all them places together.
Oh, sorry. I know what you're talking about. Yes.

And I says, "Yeah." So he says, "I'll pay you five dollars a night." Which was pretty good bread, I'll tell ya! Because I think we was playing for three dollars a day in this thing. So I said, "Sure." So I told my brother Frank, and I said, "Just tell Papa I ain't comin' back." Frank said, "Well, we might have a job..." I said, "To heck with the job, man. You haven't got no job in Baton Rouge gonna pay me any five dollars a night." So that was my start with the Martel band.
